questions.question: A 28-year-old trauma patient suffers a deep laceration to the third part of the axillary artery. Which of the following branches directly originates from this specific section of the axillary artery?

A patient is unable to initiate abduction of the arm at the shoulder joint (0–15 degrees) following a sports injury, but can complete abduction once the arm is passively raised past 15 degrees. Which nerve is most likely injured?

During a neurovascular assessment in a patient with cavernous sinus thrombosis, the physician evaluates structures passing through the sinus. Which of the following nerves travels directly through the center of the cavernous sinus adjacent to the internal carotid artery, rather than within its lateral wall?

During a thoracoabdominal procedure, the surgical team identifies the esophageal hiatus of the diaphragm located at the level of the T10 vertebra. Which of the following non-vascular structures passes through this specific aperture alongside the esophagus?

A patient presents with hyperacusis (unusual sensitivity to everyday sounds) following a lesion to the facial nerve (CN VII). Loss of motor innervation to which muscle of the middle ear accounts for this finding?
